knowledgeKeys.title: Database API keys
knowledgeKeys.description: Create new keys limited to Knowledge access, and manage database-backed keys visible to your account, including legacy administrator-issued keys. Existing keys may have broader roles or scopes; review their metadata. New issuance here does not grant general model, console or administrator access.
knowledgeKeys.issued: Issuance was acknowledged. Save the one-time secret now; the list below is a separate metadata read.
knowledgeKeys.issueUnknown: Issuance was not confirmed. A key may already exist. No creation request was repeated.
knowledgeKeys.revokedObserved: The exact database grant is disabled in the latest metadata read. This does not remove a separately configured static credential or undo already admitted work.
knowledgeKeys.revokeReadback: Revocation was acknowledged, but disabled status could not be confirmed. Refresh metadata before deciding what to do next.
knowledgeKeys.revokeUnknown: Revocation was not confirmed. Refresh the list and inspect the exact key ID; no revocation request was repeated.
knowledgeKeys.readError: Metadata could not be loaded. Key actions are disabled until a successful refresh. This is not an empty key list.
knowledgeKeys.secretNotice: Copy this value manually into your integration’s secure credential store. It is shown only in this page’s memory and disappears on dismissal, navigation or account change. The full value cannot be recovered from metadata.
knowledgeKeys.dismissSecret: I saved it; hide the secret
knowledgeKeys.name: Name
knowledgeKeys.writeScope: Also allow knowledge:write (create or modify Knowledge resources within existing access)
knowledgeKeys.uncertaintyNotice: Refresh and inspect key IDs, owners, creation times and scopes. Matching names do not prove which request created a key. You may explicitly revoke an unwanted key. Creating another key is a new grant, not recovery of the missing secret.
knowledgeKeys.allowNewDecision: I reviewed the list; allow a separate new key
knowledgeKeys.newDecision: You may review a separate new grant. The previous uncertain request has not been resolved or undone.
knowledgeKeys.createImpact: This creates a new credential with the displayed scope and expiry. Issuance has no idempotent recovery: if a response is lost, inspect metadata before deciding to create another key, including after reloading this page. Confirm only when you are ready to save its one-time value.
knowledgeKeys.revokeImpact: Disable this exact database grant and retain its metadata. This does not remove a separately configured static credential, change gateway authentication configuration, or prove rejection on every request path. Already admitted work is not undone. This action cannot restore the secret or re-enable the grant.
knowledgeKeys.listTitle: Database keys visible to your account
knowledgeKeys.listScope: The server returns keys in your current tenant: your own keys, or other owners’ keys when your server-resolved roles contain admin. This is not global administrator access. Inactive and legacy database keys are included. Enabled is a stored flag, not proof of validity. Scopes and roles are metadata, not a complete effective-access calculation; dataset permissions and server policy still apply. No complete credential is shown.
knowledgeKeys.empty: No keys were returned for your current access.
knowledgeKeys.manageDatabase: Manage database keys and review revocation
knowledgeKeys.configBoundary: This configuration list may include other tenants or runtime-only entries. Open database key management to read the keys your current tenant and owner policy permits; select the exact ID returned there. Static configuration and runtime-array keys cannot be revoked there. Disabling a database grant does not remove a separately configured static credential.

apiKey.title: API Key Authentication
apiKey.enableDesc: Authenticate via API Key in Header

recovery.scope: These are the API’s runtime metadata and startup settings, not proof of active authentication enforcement. Saving changes runtime metadata only; startup configuration, restart persistence and effective validator behavior are not changed or verified here. Concurrent edits between the check and save cannot be locked by this API.
recovery.secretConfigured: Runtime reports a configured JWT secret.
recovery.secretMissing: Runtime reports no configured JWT secret.
recovery.secretNotice: Write-only replacement. Leave blank to retain the existing secret. It is cleared after submission; metadata cannot verify the exact secret. After an uncertain save, read and review before entering a fresh replacement.
recovery.loadFailed: Authentication settings could not be read. Any values shown are from the last successful read. Your unsubmitted input is kept; refresh before saving.
recovery.saved: Save acknowledged and non-secret runtime fields matched the read-back. This does not verify the secret value, active authentication enforcement or persistence after restart.
recovery.saveUnknown: The save outcome is unknown and may already have changed runtime metadata. Your non-secret draft is kept; submitted secret input was cleared. Refresh and explicitly adopt or review the current metadata before another save. No write is retried automatically.
recovery.readBackFailed: The save was acknowledged, but read-back failed. Your non-secret draft is kept and secret input was cleared. Refresh and review before another save.
recovery.readBackChanged: The save was acknowledged, but runtime metadata does not match the submitted fields. Your non-secret draft is kept. Review the current values; no write is repeated automatically.
recovery.conflict: Runtime metadata changed since you started editing. Adopt the current values or review your draft against this new baseline before saving.
recovery.invalid: Use a nonempty HTTP header name without spaces or control characters. Enabling JWT requires an existing configured secret or a new write-only replacement.

loadBalancer.loadFailed: Could not read the current strategy. Any value shown is the last successful read. Your draft is retained; refresh before saving.
loadBalancer.saved: Save accepted and the requested strategy was read back.
loadBalancer.saveUnknown: The save response was not confirmed. The strategy may already have changed. Your draft is retained; review the latest read-back before another save.
loadBalancer.readBackFailed: Save accepted, but read-back failed. Your draft is retained. Refresh to check the current strategy; do not assume it is active yet.
loadBalancer.readBackChanged: Save accepted, but read-back differs from your selection. Another change may have occurred. Review the current value before saving again.
loadBalancer.conflict: The current strategy changed after this draft began. Your selection has been kept. Use the current value or explicitly review your draft against it.

impact.title: Review capability changes
impact.definitions: Compare visible capability descriptors by tool name. Added and removed mean entering or leaving the proposed lifecycle selection; changed means identity, version, schema, category, risk, effect or permission metadata differs. Unchanged describes metadata only.
impact.unknownBaseline: The previous effective descriptor set cannot be established from this catalog. Historical or deployment-default behavior is unknown; proposed tools are not classified as safe additions.
impact.unknownTarget: The proposed version is unavailable. Refresh the catalog before enabling it.
impact.empty: No visible capabilities in this selection.
impact.disabled: This change disables admission through this plugin selection.
impact.scope: This review covers only descriptors visible to your current authority. Hidden capabilities and affected Agent references are not enumerated. Current availability includes the existing lifecycle policy and does not predict availability after saving. Selection does not grant permissions, approve actions, cancel in-flight tools or certify safety.
impact.acknowledge: I reviewed this exact selection, the visible changes and the stated unknowns.

pluginRegistry.description: Inspect deployment-registered plugin versions and manage tenant-local version selection and enablement.
pluginRegistry.policyNotice: Version selection only restricts the existing deployment catalog. It never downloads packages, grants permissions or bypasses tool policy and approvals. Changes affect future catalog admission; already-admitted turns are not cancelled.
pluginRegistry.versionNote: Version labels are exact catalog identifiers; no latest-version or upgrade ordering is inferred.
pluginRegistry.filterHint: Try another search or clear the availability filter.
pluginRegistry.emptyHint: The catalog currently exposes no plugin-attributed capabilities to your account. Bundled capability support or a package directory alone does not mean a plugin is installed.

status.version_unavailable: Selected version is no longer registered

lifecycle.enableForTenant: Enable selected version for this tenant
lifecycle.missingVersion: An unavailable version can remain disabled. Select a registered version before enabling.
lifecycle.effectNotice: Only the selected version remains eligible for future catalog admission. Existing permission, tool-policy and approval restrictions still apply. No package is downloaded and no active execution is cancelled.
lifecycle.adminOnly: Tenant lifecycle changes require administrator authority.
lifecycle.savedRefreshFailed: Configuration was saved, but its refreshed state could not be loaded. Refresh before making another change.
lifecycle.conflict: The plugin configuration or deployment catalog changed. Refresh and review the current state before saving again.
lifecycle.forbidden: Your current authority cannot change this plugin selection. Refresh to check your access.
lifecycle.uncertain: The save could not be confirmed. It may have committed; refresh and check the recorded revision before retrying.
lifecycle.hiddenSelection: Version not visible to this account

tenantGovernance.title: Tenant governance
tenantGovernance.description: Manage stored tenant tool policies and investigate tool execution records through the existing Gateway administration API.
tenantGovernance.scopeNotice: Administrator access covers all tenants. This page shows stored policies and recorded tool executions; it does not certify runtime enforcement, audit completeness or retention.
tenantGovernance.emptyPolicyHint: Only explicit stored policies appear here. An absent policy is not evidence that tools are disabled.
tenantGovernance.writeNotice: Saving replaces the editable policy fields for this tenant, including an existing policy with the same ID. There is no version-conflict check. Other stored fields are retained.
tenantGovernance.tenantHint: Use 1–64 alphanumeric characters, hyphens or underscores. The server validates the exact tenant identifier.
tenantGovernance.listHint: Enter a JSON array of tool or category names, or null. For example: ["search", "retrieve"]. Null and [] are preserved exactly. Do not enter secrets.
tenantGovernance.saveError: The save could not be verified. The policy may already have been stored. Close this editor and refresh the policy list before deciding whether to submit again.
tenantGovernance.saved: Policy for {tenant} saved and read back successfully.
tenantGovernance.auditNotice: Tenant and user filters are exact matches; tool name is a case-sensitive substring. Rows and totals are separate reads and may change during pagination. Raw inputs and error text are not displayed. These are tool executions, not configuration-change audit records.
tenantGovernance.noAudit: No tool execution records on this page.

validation.tenant: Enter a tenant ID between 1 and 64 characters.
validation.list: Each policy list must be null or a JSON array containing only strings.
validation.rate: Calls per minute must be an integer from 1 to 10,000.

configAudit.notice: Exact-match filters. Actor tenant is the tenant recorded for the administrator who made the change; it may differ from the affected resource’s tenant. Records are newest first; concurrent changes can shift offset pages.
configAudit.coverage: Only persisted config_changed events are shown. Some changes, including tenant tool-policy writes, do not emit these events. Empty results do not establish audit completeness or retention. Configuration snapshots, raw summaries, IP addresses and error details are excluded.
configAudit.bound: The browsing limit has been reached. Narrow the filters to find more specific records.
configAudit.empty: No recorded configuration changes on this page.

auth.passwordChangeUnknown: The password change result is unknown. It may have succeeded. Sign in again to check; contact your administrator if you cannot sign in.

tenantMcp.notice: Manage stored tenant MCP server allowlists and connection limits. Saving a policy does not prove that a server is connected or that a running worker has applied it.
tenantMcp.writeNotice: This replaces the selected tenant’s allowlist and connection limit. Current values are checked before saving, but the API does not provide atomic conflict protection.
tenantMcp.overridesPreserved: Existing server overrides are preserved without displaying their values. This form does not edit endpoints or credentials.
tenantMcp.serversHint: Enter a JSON array of server IDs, for example ["docs"]. An empty array is saved exactly as entered; null is not accepted. Runtime policy behavior remains server-owned.
tenantMcp.saved: MCP policy for {tenant} was saved and read back successfully.
tenantMcp.empty: No tenant MCP policies are configured.
tenantMcp.saveError: The policy could have changed or the save/readback could have failed. A write may already have committed. Close this editor, refresh the list, and review the current policy before trying again.

validation.tenant: Enter a tenant ID of 1–64 characters. An existing policy’s tenant cannot be changed.
validation.list: Enter a JSON array containing only server ID strings.
validation.connections: Enter a whole-number connection limit from 1 to 100.

roleManagement.title: Roles and permissions
roleManagement.scope: Role definitions are shared across the platform, not limited to your tenant. Creating a role does not assign it to anyone.
roleManagement.readOnly: You can inspect the catalog. Creating shared roles requires current platform-administrator authority and role:create permission.
roleManagement.readFailed: The current role or permission catalog could not be read. Refresh before creating a role.
roleManagement.confirmed: The create response was accepted and the current role definition matches the submitted fields.
roleManagement.matchesUnknown: The current definition matches your submission, but the create response was not confirmed. This does not prove that your request created the role.
roleManagement.differs: A role with this name exists, but its current definition differs. Review it with a platform administrator; no second create was sent.
roleManagement.absentUnknown: This read did not find the submitted name. That does not prove the create failed; do not replay it without operator reconciliation.
roleManagement.readbackFailed: The current definition could not be verified. Keep the submitted name and use read-only recovery.
roleManagement.exists: That role name already exists. Nothing was created. Refresh and choose a different name.
roleManagement.catalogChanged: The permission catalog changed. Refresh and review the selected permissions again.
roleManagement.preflightFailed: The pre-submit checks failed. No create was sent. Refresh and review again.
roleManagement.uncertainty: Save this name before leaving. Recovery here only reads this exact name and never resends creation. Matching metadata does not verify all permission-table writes, cache propagation, or effective access.
roleManagement.assignmentNotice: Before assigning, review the current definition. Use the existing user editor to select the role and save. The server rechecks account-management authority; assignment does not prove effective access.
roleManagement.name: Role name
roleManagement.nameHint: Use 1–100 lowercase letters or underscores. The name permissions is reserved by the existing permission-catalog route.
roleManagement.emptyPermissions: No permissions selected. This role grants no catalog permissions by itself.
roleManagement.reviewNotice: Only the listed permissions will be submitted. Existing roles are not changed. Confirmation sends one create request after read-only catalog and name checks; these checks are not a concurrency lock.
roleManagement.denied: Role catalog access requires role:list permission.
roleManagement.invalid: Enter a valid lowercase role name and a description of 1–255 characters.
roleManagement.reserved: The name permissions is unavailable here because GET /roles/permissions is the permission catalog, not exact-role recovery. Choose another name; existing roles are unchanged.
